author: Drunken Robot
content: Repentance is 20* yards which makes this dance especially dangerous. Ideally in a map like WSG, you'd be on flag defense and kiting them away from the FC or towards defenders who can capitalize on the pressure you're providing (like a mage). If the pally steps on a trap or gets improved consuss, you need to immediately viper+MS+cheetah and walk back a bit before they BoF themselves. If they're clever, they'll then cleanse the viper sting, but they will end up net-negative on mana since they burned 2 spells and ate 2 ticks.

author: Forlorn Shade
content:
Not quite. Mixed result.

If you analyze case by case then you will come to the conclusion it's more often a hindrance to them than it is beneficial.

Classes that couldn't remove... everything, would be more counterable by Rogues. Classes that already could remove parts of their control kit... now do so even more. That includes even enemy Rogues.

Meanwhile, Rogues themselves are supposed to be control/setup machines relying on that characteristic to get kills or at least to harass teams to tip the scales for their own. They are not like Enhancement Shamans in which case they just walk in and smack something and by chance that something might just outright die.

Rogue relies on CC. This hurts that.

Classes that don't rely on CC and just mindlessly pump got a buff and are less prone to getting ganked by Rogues regardless of what their original Trinket before this change could do.

Classes that already have so little CC that it becomes important are also set back by this, because now chances are it'll just be removed when otherwise it might not actually be removable (depending on what the enemy Class is).

It's overall more negative than positive. It feeds into this mindless burst meta that's less about strategy and more about just mashing keys.

It's a hard balance -- if you keep and encourage these sort of features, you get a much higher barrier of entry. For every 5 players, you'll get one looking up a guide, one trying to learn, and three who decide they don't want to play WSG again. 

So do we design for the minority who enjoy it, and slowly let the mode wither and shrink? That answer sucks.
